translations.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
The earth was formless and empty, and darkness covered the surface of the deep. The Spirit of God hovered over the surface of the waters.
God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
God saw that the light was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.
God called the light day, and he called the darkness night. There was evening, and there was morning—one day.
God said, “Let there be an expanse between the waters, separating water from water.”
God made the expanse and separated the waters below the expanse from the waters above the expanse. And it was so.
God called the expanse heaven. There was evening and there was morning, the second day.
God said, “Let the waters below the heavens gather into one place, and let the dry land appear.” And it was so.
God called the dry land earth, and he called the gathered waters seas. God saw that it was good.

God said, “Let the earth produce vegetation: plants yielding seed according to their kinds, and fruit trees bearing fruit according to their kinds, with their seed in them, on the earth.” And it was so.
The earth produced vegetation: plants yielding seed according to their kinds, and trees bearing fruit with their seed in it, according to their kinds. God saw that it was good.
There was evening and there was morning, the third day.
God said, “Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to separate day from night. Let them serve as signs and mark seasons, days, and years.
Let them shine in the expanse of the heavens to give light on the earth.” And it was so.
God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the smaller light to rule the night, and the stars.
God placed them in the expanse of the heavens to give light on the earth.
And to rule over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. God saw that it was good.
There was evening and there was morning, the fourth day.
God said, “Let the waters swarm with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the expanse of the heavens.”

God created the great sea monsters and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarmed, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. God saw that it was good.
God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth.”
There was evening and there was morning, the fifth day.
God said, “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, crawling creatures, and wild animals of the earth according to their kinds.” And it was so.

God made the wild animals of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and all the creatures that crawl on the earth according to their kinds. God saw that it was good.

God said, “Let us make human beings in our image, according to our likeness. Let them rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the livestock, all the wild animals of the earth, and every creature that crawls on the earth.”
God created Adam in his image. In the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.

God blessed them, and God said to them, “Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the heavens, the livestock, and every living creature that moves on the earth.”
God said, “Look, I have given you every seed-bearing plant that grows across the whole earth, and every tree bearing fruit whose seed can be sown. They shall be food for you.
And to all the wild animals, all the birds of the heavens, and everything that moves on the earth and has life in it, all green plants for food.” And it was so.
God saw everything he had made, and it was very good. There was evening, and there was morning: the sixth day.
The heavens and the earth were completed, with everything in them.
On the sixth day God finished the work he had done, and on the seventh day he rested from all the work he had done.
God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the work he had done in creating.
These are the origins of the heavens and the earth when they were created, when the Lord God made the heavens and the earth.

None of the trees of the field were yet on the earth, and none of the plants of the field had yet sprouted, because the Lord God had not sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.
A spring rose from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.
The Lord God formed Adam from dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and Adam became a living being.
The Lord God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and placed Adam, whom he had formed, there.

The Lord God caused every tree that was pleasing to look at and good for food to grow from the ground, with the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided into four branches.
The name of the first is Pishon. It flows around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
The gold of that land is good. Bdellium and beryl stones are there.
The name of the second river is Gihon. It flows around the whole land of Cush.
The name of the third river is Tigris. It flows opposite Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
The Lord God took Adam and placed him in the garden of Eden to cultivate it and care for it.
The Lord God commanded Adam, saying to him, “You may freely eat from every tree in the garden.
But you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, because on the day you eat from it, you will certainly die.”
The Lord God said, “It is not good for Adam to be alone. I will make him a helper like him.”
The Lord God formed from the ground every wild animal and every bird of the sky, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. Whatever Adam called each living creature became its name.
Adam gave names to all the livestock, all the birds of the sky, and all the animals of the earth. But for Adam no helper like him was found.
The Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, and he slept. He took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place.
The Lord God fashioned the rib he had taken from Adam into a woman and brought her to Adam.
Adam said, “This time, here is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. She will be called woman, because she was taken from man.”
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and join himself to his wife, and the two of them will become one flesh.
Both of them, Adam and his wife, were naked, and they were not ashamed.
The serpent was more cunning than any of the wild animals the Lord God had made. The serpent said to the woman, “Did God really say that you must not eat from any of the trees in the garden?”
The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from all the trees in the garden.
But concerning the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, ‘You must not eat from it or go near it, or you will die.’”
The serpent said to the woman, “You certainly will not die.
For God knows that on the day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like gods, knowing good and evil.”

The woman saw that the tree was good for food, that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable to look at. She took some of its fruit and ate it. She also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate.
The eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked. They joined fig leaves together and made coverings for themselves.
They heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden toward evening, and Adam and his wife hid from the LORD God among the trees in the garden.
The LORD God called to Adam and said to him, “Where are you, Adam?”
He said, “I heard your sound in the garden, and I saw that I was naked, so I hid.”
The LORD said to him, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”
Adam said, “The woman you gave to be with me—she gave me some from the tree, and I ate.”
The LORD God said to the woman, “What is this you have done?” The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”
The LORD God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, you are cursed more than all livestock and all wild animals. You will crawl on your belly and eat dust all the days of your life.
I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers. He will trample your head, and you will strike him on his heel.”
To the woman he said, “I will greatly increase your pain and your pregnancies. In pain you will give birth to children. You will turn toward your husband, and he will rule over you.”

To Adam he said, “Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree about which I commanded you, saying, ‘You must not eat from it,’ the ground is cursed because of you. Through painful toil you will eat from it all the days of your life.
It will grow thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
By the sweat of your face you will eat bread until you return to the ground from which you were taken. For you are dust, and to dust you will return.”
Adam named his wife Eve, because she was the mother of everyone living.
The LORD God made tunics of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.
The LORD God said, “Look, Adam has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat and live forever—”
The Lord God sent him out of the garden of Eden to cultivate the ground from which he had been taken.
The LORD God drove him out and stationed a cherub and the blade of a whirling sword east of the garden of Eden to guard the way to the tree of life.
Adam had sexual relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. She said, “I have acquired a man for the LORD.”
She gave birth again, to his brother Abel. Abel became a shepherd of sheep, and Cain became a worker of the ground.
After some time, Cain brought some of the produce of his ground as an offering to the LORD.
Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock, the fattest of them. The LORD was pleased with Abel and his offering.
But he was not pleased with Cain and his offering. Cain was very upset, and his face grew gloomy.
The LORD said to Cain, “Why are you upset, and why has your face grown gloomy?”
Look, if you do well, you will be accepted. But if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door. You will turn toward it, and it will rule over you.
Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let us go out to the plain.” While they were in the field, Cain rose against his brother Abel and killed him.
The Lord said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” He said, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”
The Lord said to him, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to me from the ground.
Now you are cursed from the ground, which opened its mouth and received your brother’s blood from your hands.
When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its strength to you. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth.”
Cain said to the Lord, “My sin is too great to be forgiven.
Look, today you have driven me from the face of the ground, and I will be hidden from your presence. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me.”
The Lord said to him, “Not so! Whoever kills Cain will suffer sevenfold retribution.” The Lord put a mark on Cain so that whoever found him would not kill him.
Cain went out from the Lord’s presence and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Cain had sexual relations with his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. He was building a city, and he named the city Enoch after his son.
Irad was born to Enoch. Irad fathered Mehujael, Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
Lamech took two wives for himself. The name of one was Adah, and the name of the other was Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal. He was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock.
His brother’s name was Jubal. He was the father of all who play the lyre and the harp.
Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-cain, a craftsman in every kind of bronze and iron work. Tubal-cain’s sister was Naamah.
Lamech said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my words. For I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for bruising me.
If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold.”
Adam again had sexual relations with his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Seth, saying, “God has given me another offspring in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.”
A son was also born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. Then he began to call on the name of the Lord.
This is the book of Adam’s descendants. When God created Adam, he made him in the likeness of God.
He created them male and female. God blessed them and named them Adam on the day he created them.
Adam lived 130 years and fathered a son in his likeness, according to his image, and named him Seth.
After fathering Seth, Adam lived eight hundred years and fathered sons and daughters.
Adam’s entire life lasted nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
Seth lived one hundred and five years and fathered Enosh.
After fathering Enosh, Seth lived eight hundred and seven years and fathered sons and daughters.
Seth’s entire life lasted nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
Enosh lived ninety years and fathered Kenan.
After he fathered Kenan, Enosh lived eight hundred and fifteen years and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died.
Kenan lived seventy years and fathered Mahalalel.
After he fathered Mahalalel, Kenan lived eight hundred and forty years and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Kenan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.
Mahalalel lived sixty-five years and fathered Jared.
After he fathered Jared, Mahalalel lived eight hundred and thirty years and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Mahalalel were 895 years, and he died.
Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years and fathered Enoch.
After he fathered Enoch, Jared lived eight hundred years and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.
Enoch lived sixty-five years and fathered Methuselah.
After he fathered Methuselah, Enoch pleased God for three hundred years and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.
Enoch pleased God, and he was no longer there, because God took him.
Methuselah lived one hundred and eighty-seven years and fathered Lamech.
After he fathered Lamech, Methuselah lived seven hundred and eighty-two years and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Methuselah were 969 years, and he died.
Lamech lived one hundred and eighty-two years and fathered a son.
He named him Noah and said, “This one will comfort us in our work and the toil of our hands, and from the ground that the Lord cursed.”
After he fathered Noah, Lamech lived five hundred and ninety-five years and fathered sons and daughters.
All the days of Lamech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died.
Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
When human beings began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them,
the sons of God saw that the daughters of humans were beautiful, and they took wives for themselves from all whom they chose.
The Lord said, “My spirit will not dwell in humans forever, because they are flesh. Their days will be one hundred and twenty years.”
There were giants on the earth in those days, and also afterward, because the sons of God went in to the daughters of men, and they bore them giants—the giants of ancient times, giants of renown.
The Lord saw that human wickedness had become great on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was evil every day.
The Lord regretted that he had made humankind on the earth, and he was grieved in his heart.
The Lord said, “I will wipe the human beings I have created from the face of the earth, along with the livestock, the crawling creatures, and the birds of the sky, because I regret that I made them.”
But Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord.
This is the account of Noah's descendants. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and Noah pleased God.
Noah fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The earth became corrupt before God, and the earth was filled with injustice.
God saw that the earth was corrupt, because all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
God said to Noah, “The end of all flesh has come before me, because the earth is filled with injustice because of them. Look, I am going to destroy them along with the earth.
Make yourself an ark of boxwood. Make compartments in the ark, and coat it inside and outside with pitch.
This is how you are to make it: the ark is to be three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
Make [?] for the ark, and finish it to a cubit at the top. Put the ark's door in its side. Make it with a lower deck, a second deck, and a third deck.
Look, I myself am bringing a flood of water over the earth to destroy all flesh under heaven that has the breath of life in it. Everything on the earth will perish.
But I will establish my covenant with you. You will enter the ark—you, your sons, your wife, and your sons' wives with you.
Bring into the ark two of every living thing, of all flesh, to keep them alive with you. They are to be male and female.
Of the birds according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and all the crawling creatures of the earth according to their kinds, two of each will enter with you to be kept alive.
As for you, take some of every kind of food that is eaten and store it with you. It will be food for you and for them.”
Noah did everything God commanded him; that is what he did.
God said to Noah, “Enter the ark, you and your whole household, because I have seen that you are righteous before me in this generation.
Take with you seven each of all the clean animals, males and females, and two each of the animals that are not clean, males and females.
Also take seven each of the birds of the sky, males and females, to keep their offspring alive over the face of the whole earth.
For in seven days I will send rain down on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe every living thing I have made from the face of the earth.”
Noah did everything the Lord commanded him.
Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of water came upon the earth.
Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives went into the ark with him to escape the floodwaters.
From the clean animals and the animals that were not clean, from the birds, and from everything that crawls on the earth,
they went into the ark with Noah two by two, males and females, as God had commanded Noah.
After seven days, the floodwaters came upon the earth.

In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that very day, all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the floodgates of heaven were opened.
Rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On that very day Noah, along with Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah’s sons, Noah’s wife, and the three wives of his sons, went into the ark.

They and every wild animal according to its kind, every domestic animal according to its kind, every crawling creature that crawls on the earth according to its kinds, every flying creature according to its kind, every bird and every winged creature,
went into the ark with Noah, two by two, from all flesh in which there was the spirit of life.
Those that entered went in as males and females from all flesh, as God had commanded him. And the Lord shut him in.
The flood continued on the earth for forty days. The waters increased and lifted the ark, and it rose above the earth.
The waters grew strong and increased greatly over the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the waters.
The waters grew very, very strong over the earth, and all the high mountains under the whole sky were covered.
The waters rose fifteen cubits higher, and the mountains were covered.
All flesh that moved on the earth perished: birds, domestic animals, wild animals, every crawling creature that crawls on the earth, and all human beings.
Everything on dry land that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils died.

He wiped out everything that existed on the face of the earth, from human beings to domestic animals, crawling creatures, and the birds of the sky. They were wiped from the earth, and Noah and those with him in the ark were left.
The waters remained strong over the earth for one hundred and fifty days.
God remembered Noah and all the wild animals, all the domestic animals, and all the birds that were with him in the ark. God sent a wind over the earth, and the waters grew calm.
The springs of the deep and the floodgates of heaven were closed, and the rain from heaven was stopped.
The waters steadily receded from the earth, and after one hundred and fifty days the waters had decreased.
In the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Qardu.
The waters continued to decrease until the tenth month. On the first day of the tenth month, the tops of the mountains became visible.
After forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.
He sent out the raven, and it went out and did not return until the waters had dried up from the earth.
He sent out the dove from him to see whether the waters had subsided from the surface of the earth.

But the dove found no resting place for the sole of its foot, and it returned to him in the ark, because water covered the surface of the whole earth. He reached out his hand, took it, and brought it into the ark with him.
He waited another seven days and again sent the dove out of the ark.
The dove came to him in the evening, and there was an olive leaf held in its beak. Then Noah knew that the waters had receded from the surface of the earth.
He waited another seven days and sent out the dove, but the dove did not return to him again.
In the six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and the surface of the earth was dry.
In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.
God spoke to Noah and said to him:
“Come out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.

Bring out with you every living creature that is with you, of every kind of flesh: birds, livestock, and every crawling creature that crawls on the earth. Let them breed on the earth, be fruitful, and multiply on the earth.”
Noah came out, along with his wife, his sons, and his sons’ wives.
All the wild animals, all the livestock, all the birds, and everything that crawls on the earth came out of the ark by their families.
Noah built an altar to the LORD. He took some of every kind of clean animal and every kind of clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

The LORD smelled the aroma of [?], a soothing aroma. The LORD said in his heart, “I will never again curse the earth because of humanity, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. Nor will I ever again strike down every living thing as I have done.
From now on, as long as the earth endures, sowing and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will not cease.”
God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.
Fear and dread of you will fall upon every animal of the earth, every bird of the sky, and everything with which the earth teems. All the fish of the sea will be delivered into your hands.
Every moving creature that lives will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.
But you must not eat flesh with its life, its blood, still in it.
And I will indeed demand an accounting for your lifeblood. From every animal I will demand it, and from a human being. From a man and his brother I will demand an accounting for a human life.
Whoever sheds human blood, by a human being shall his blood be shed, because Adam was made in the image of God.
And you, be fruitful and multiply; have offspring on the earth and multiply on it.”
God said to Noah and to his sons with him:
“Look, I am establishing my covenant with you and with your descendants after you.

And with every living creature that is with you—with the birds, with the livestock, and with every wild animal of the earth that is with you—with all those that came out of the ark, and with every wild animal of the earth.
I will establish my covenant with you: never again will all flesh perish by the waters of a flood, and never again will there be a flood to destroy the earth.”
God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I am giving between me and you and every living creature with you, for all generations forever.
I have set my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
When I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears in the clouds,
I will remember my covenant between me and you, and with every living creature that is with you, and with all flesh. Never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh.
The rainbow will be in the clouds, and I will look at it to remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh on the earth.
God said to Noah, “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between me and all flesh on the earth.”
The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were Noah’s sons, and from these people spread throughout the whole earth.
Noah began working the ground and planted a vineyard.
He drank some of its wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent.
Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father’s nakedness and told his two brothers.

Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it across both their shoulders, and walked backward to cover their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.
Noah awoke from his wine and learned everything his youngest son had done to him.
He said, “Cursed be Canaan! He will be a slave of slaves to his brothers.”
He also said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be their slave.
May God enlarge Japheth, and may he live in Shem’s tent, and let Canaan be their slave.”
Noah lived 350 years after the flood.
All the days of Noah’s life were 950 years, and he died.
These are the family lines of Noah’s sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
The sons of Japheth were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Diphar, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Doranim.
From these they spread out among the islands of the nations in their lands, each according to his language, according to their clans within their nations.
The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were Sheba and Daran.
Cush fathered Nimrod. He began to be a mighty man on the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the Lord. That is why people say, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the Lord.”
The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Akkad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land the Assyrian went out and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah,
and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah. That is the great city.
Mizraim fathered Ludim, [?], Lehabim, and Naphtuhim.
And Pathrusim and Casluhim, from whom the Philistines and Cappadocians came.
Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and the Hittites,
and the Jebusites, Amorites, and Girgashites,
and the Hivites, Arkites, and Sinites,
and the Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites. Afterward the clans of the Canaanites scattered.
The territory of the Canaanites extended from Sidon toward Gerar, as far as Gaza, and toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
These are the descendants of Ham, according to their clans and languages, in their lands and nations.
Shem also had children. He was the ancestor of all the descendants of Eber and the brother of Japheth the elder.
The sons of Shem were Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
The sons of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
Two sons were born to Eber. One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided. His brother was named Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
and Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah,
and Obal, Abimael, and Sheba,
and Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were sons of Joktan.
Their settlement extended from Manasseh toward Sepharvaim, the mountain in the east.
These are the descendants of Shem, according to their clans and languages, in their lands and nations.
These are the clans of Noah’s sons, according to their genealogies and clans, in their nations. From these the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.
The whole earth had one language and one form of speech.
As they traveled from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
They said to one another, “Come, let us make bricks and burn them in the fire.” They used brick for stone and lime for mortar.
They said, “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, and let us make a name for ourselves, so that we will not be scattered over the face of the whole earth.”
The Lord came down to see the city and the tower that the people were building.
The Lord said, “Look, they are one people, and they all have one language, and this is what they have planned to do. From now on, nothing they plan to do will be beyond their reach.”
“Come, let us go down and divide the languages there, so that no one will understand the language of his fellow.”
The Lord scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.
Therefore he called its name Babel, because there the Lord confused the languages of the whole earth. From there the Lord scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
These are the descendants of Shem. When Shem was one hundred years old, he fathered Arpachshad, two years after the flood.
After fathering Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 years and fathered sons and daughters.
Arpachshad lived thirty-five years and fathered Shelah.
After he fathered Shelah, Arpachshad lived four hundred and three years and fathered sons and daughters.
Shelah lived thirty years and fathered Eber.
After he fathered Eber, Shelah lived four hundred and three years and fathered sons and daughters.
Eber lived thirty-four years and fathered Peleg.
After he fathered Peleg, Eber lived four hundred and thirty years and fathered sons and daughters.
Peleg lived thirty years and fathered Reu.
After he fathered Reu, Peleg lived two hundred and nine years and fathered sons and daughters.
Reu lived thirty-two years and fathered Serug.
After he fathered Serug, Reu lived two hundred and seven years and fathered sons and daughters.
Serug lived thirty years and fathered Nahor.
After he fathered Nahor, Serug lived two hundred years and fathered sons and daughters.
Nahor lived twenty-nine years and fathered Terah.
After he fathered Terah, Nahor lived one hundred and nineteen years and fathered sons and daughters.
Terah lived seventy-five years and fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
These are the descendants of Terah. Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.
Haran died during the lifetime of his father Terah, in the land where he was born, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sarai, and Nahor’s wife was named Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah and Iscah.
Sarai was barren and had no children.

Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot, the son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, the wife of his son Abram. They went out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. They came as far as Haran and settled there.
Terah lived for 205 years, and Terah died in Haran.
The Lord said to Abram, “Leave your land, the place where you were born, and your father’s household, and go to the land that I will show you.
I will make you into a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed.
I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse those who curse you. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you and through your descendants.”
Abram did as the Lord had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all the possessions they had acquired, and the people they had acquired in Haran. They set out for the land of Canaan and came to the land of Canaan.
Abram passed through the land as far as the site of Shechem, as far as the oak of Mamre. The Canaanites were still living in the land.
The Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I will give this land to your descendants.” He built an altar there to the Lord, who had appeared to him.
He moved from there to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. He built an altar there to the Lord and called on the name of the Lord.
Abram set out and continued on his journey toward the south.
There was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt to stay there, because the famine was very severe in the land.
As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, “Look, I know that you are a beautiful woman.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife.’ They will kill me but keep you alive.
Say, ‘I am his sister,’ so that things will go well for me because of you, and my life will be spared because of you.”
When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that his wife was very beautiful.
Pharaoh’s officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
He treated Abram well because of her, and Abram came to have sheep, cattle, male donkeys, male and female slaves, female donkeys, and camels.
The Lord struck Pharaoh and the members of his household with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
Pharaoh summoned Abram and said to him, “What is this you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Now, here is your wife. Take her and go.”
Pharaoh gave men orders concerning him, and they sent him away with his wife and everything he had.
Abram went up from Egypt toward the south, with his wife and everything he had, and Lot went with him.
Abram was very rich in possessions, silver, and gold.
He traveled in stages from the south as far as Bethel, to the place where he had pitched his tent before, between Bethel and Ai.
to the site of the altar he had made there at first. There Abram called on the name of the Lord.
Lot, who traveled with Abram, also had sheep, cattle, and very many tents.
That land could not support them living together, because their possessions were very great, and they could not live together.
There was a quarrel between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. The Canaanites and the Perizzites were still living in the land.
Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no quarrel between you and me, or between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, because we are brothers.
Look, the whole land is before you. Separate yourself from me. If you go to the right, I will go to the left; if you go to the left, I will go to the right.”

Lot looked up and saw the whole land of the Jordan, that it was all well watered. Before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, it was like the garden of God, and like the land of Egypt as you approach Zoan.
Lot chose for himself the whole land of the Jordan. Lot set out from the east, and they separated from each other.
Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lot lived in the towns of the plain and took possession as far as Sodom.
The people of Sodom were very wicked and sinful before the Lord.
After Lot had separated from him, the Lord said to Abram, “Look up from the place where you are, and look north, south, east, and west.
For I will give all the land you see to you and your descendants forever.
I will make your descendants like the dust of the earth, so that if you can count the dust of the earth, your descendants too can be counted.
Get up and walk through the length and breadth of the land, for I will give it to you.”
Abram came and settled by the oak of Mamre the Amorite, in Hebron. There he built an altar to the Lord.
In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of the Gilites,
they made war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.
All these gathered in the Valley of the Sodomites, which is the Salt Sea.
For twelve years they had served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings with him came and defeated the giants at Ashteroth-karnaim, the mighty men among them, and the Emim at Shaveh-kiriathaim,
and the Horites in the mountains of Seir, as far as the terebinth of Paran in the wilderness.
They turned back and came to En-mishpat, which is Rekem, and devastated all the territories of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who lived in En-gedi.
The king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar, went out. All these fought in the Valley of the Sodomites
against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of the Gilites, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar—four kings against five.
The Valley of the Sodomites was full of tar pits. The king of Sodom and the king of Gomorrah fled and fell there, while those who remained fled to the mountains.
They took all the possessions of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and went away.
They took Lot, Abram’s nephew, and his possessions and went away. He had been living in Sodom.
Someone who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. He was living among the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Aner and Eshcol. They were Abram’s allies.
When Abram heard that his nephew had been taken captive, he armed the young men born in his household, three hundred and eighteen of them, and pursued them as far as Dan.
He and his servants split up to attack them at night. They defeated them and pursued them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
They brought back all the possessions. He also brought back his nephew Lot and his possessions, as well as the women and the people.
The king of Sodom came out to meet him after he returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, in the Valley of Shaveh, which is the Valley of the Kings.
Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of God Most High.
He blessed him and said, “Blessed be Abram by God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth.”
“Blessed is God Most High, who delivered your enemies into your hands.” And he gave him a tenth of everything.
The king of Sodom said to Abram, “Give me the people, and take the possessions for yourself.”
Abram said to the king of Sodom, “I have raised my hands to God Most High, to whom heaven and earth belong,
that I will not take so much as a thread or a sandal strap, or anything that belongs to you, so that you cannot say, ‘I made Abram rich.’
Except for what the young men have eaten and the shares of the men who went with me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre—let them take their shares.”
After these things, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, and he said to him, “Do not be afraid, Abram. I will help you. Your reward is very great.”
Abram said, “Lord God, what will you give me, since I remain childless, and Eliezer of Damascus, a member of my household, will inherit from me?”
Abram said, “Look, you have given me no son, and a member of my household will inherit from me.”
And the Lord said to him, “This man will not be your heir. Instead, your own son, who comes from your body, will be your heir.”
He brought him outside and said to him, “Look at the heavens and count the stars, if you can count them.” Then he said to him, “So will your descendants be.”
Abram believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
He said to him, “I am the Lord who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess.”
Abram said, “Lord God, how will I know that I will possess it?”
He said to him, “Get a three-year-old calf, a three-year-old ram, a three-year-old goat, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”
He took all these, divided them into equal halves, and placed each piece opposite its matching piece. But he did not divide the birds.
And birds came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.
As the sun was about to set, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and terror and great darkness fell upon him.
He said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs. They will be put to work and enslaved for four hundred years.
But I will also judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will come out with great possessions.
You will be gathered to your ancestors in peace and will be buried at a good old age.
In the fourth generation they will return here, because the sins of the Amorites have not yet reached their full measure.”
The sun was setting, and darkness fell. And there was a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passing between these pieces.
On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram and said to him, “I will give this land to your descendants, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates:
the Kenites, the Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites;
the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the giants;
the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”
Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children. She had an Egyptian slave woman named Hagar.
Sarai said to Abram, “Look, the Lord has kept me from bearing children. Sleep with my slave woman; perhaps I will find comfort through her.” And Abram listened to Sarai.
After Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years, Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar, her Egyptian slave woman, and gave her to her husband Abram as a wife.
He slept with Hagar, and she became pregnant. When she saw that she was pregnant, her mistress became contemptible in her eyes.

Sarai said to Abram, “The wrong done to me is your responsibility! I put my slave woman in your arms, and when she saw that she was pregnant, I became contemptible in her eyes. May the Lord judge between me and you.”
Abram said to his wife Sarai, “Look, your slave woman is in your hands. Do to her whatever seems right to you.” Then Sarai, her mistress, treated her harshly, and she fled from her.
The angel of the Lord found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, on the road to Gadar.
He said to her, “Hagar, Sarai’s slave woman, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She said, “I am fleeing from my mistress Sarai.”
The angel of the Lord said to her, “Return to your mistress and submit to her authority.”
The angel of the Lord said to her, “I will greatly multiply your descendants, so that they cannot be counted because they are so many.”
The angel of the Lord said to her, “Look, you are pregnant and will bear a son. You shall name him Ishmael, because the Lord has heard you in your oppression.
He will be a wild donkey of a man. His hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him. He will live on the border of all his brothers.”
She called upon the name of the Lord who spoke with her and said, “You are God in a vision.” For she said, “Look, I too have seen a vision after he saw me.”
Therefore she called that well “The Well of the Living One Who Saw Me.” It is between Rekem and Gadar.
Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named his son who was born to him, whom Hagar bore him, Ishmael.
Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram.
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be pleasing before me and be blameless.
I will establish my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”
Abram fell facedown, and God spoke with him and said to him,
“As for me, look, I am establishing my covenant with you, and you will be the father of a multitude of nations.
Your name will no longer be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, because I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
I will make you fruitful and multiply you greatly. I will make you into nations, and kings will come from your own body.
I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations, as an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your descendants after you.
I will give you and your descendants after you the land where you live as a foreigner, the whole land of Canaan, as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God.
God said to Abraham, “You must keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you throughout their generations.
This is my covenant that you must keep between me and you and your descendants after you: you must circumcise every male.
You must circumcise the flesh of your foreskins, and it will be a sign of the covenant between me and you.

Every male among you must be circumcised when he is eight days old, throughout your generations, whether born in the household or bought with money from any foreigner who is not one of your descendants.
Anyone born in your household or bought with your money must certainly be circumcised. My covenant will be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
Any uncircumcised male whose foreskin is not circumcised will be destroyed from among his people. That person has broken my covenant.”
God said to Abraham, “As for Sarai your wife, you must not call her Sarai, because her name is Sarah.
I will bless her, and I will also give you a son by her. I will bless him, and he will become nations; kings of peoples will come from him.”
Abraham fell facedown and laughed. He said to himself, “Can a son be born to a man a hundred years old? Or can Sarah, who is ninety years old, give birth?”
Abraham said to God, “If only Ishmael might live before you!”
God said to Abraham, “Truly, Sarah your wife will bear you a son, and you will name him Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant, and with his descendants after him.
As for Ishmael, I have heard you. Look, I have blessed him and will multiply him and increase him greatly. He will father twelve rulers, and I will make him a great nation.
But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year.”
When he had finished speaking with him, God went up from Abraham.

Abraham took his son Ishmael and everyone born in his household and everyone bought with his money, every male among the members of Abraham’s household, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very day, as God had told him.
Abraham was ninety-nine years old when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
His son Ishmael was thirteen years old when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
That very day Abraham circumcised his son Ishmael,
and all the men of his household, those born in his household and those bought with his money, including those from among foreigners, he circumcised along with him.
The Lord appeared to him among the oaks of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance of the tent in the heat of the day.
He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of the tent to meet them and bowed down to the ground.
And he said, “Lord, if I have found favor in your eyes, do not pass by your servant.”
“Let me bring a little water. Wash your feet and rest under the tree.”
“Take a piece of bread and strengthen yourselves. Afterward you may go on, since this is why you have come to your servant.” And they said, “Do as you have said.”
Abraham hurried and ran to the tent to Sarah and said, “Quickly, take three measures of fine flour! Knead it and make cakes.”
Abraham ran to the herd and took a fine, fat calf. He gave it to the young man, who hurried to prepare it.
And he took butter, milk, and the calf he had prepared and set them before them. He stood beside them under the tree while they ate.
They said to him, “Where is Sarah your wife?” And he said, “There, in the tent.”
He said to him, “I will certainly return to you at this time, while she is alive, and Sarah your wife will have a son.” Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, and he was behind her.
Abraham and Sarah were old and advanced in years. Sarah had stopped having her monthly periods.
Sarah laughed to herself and said, “After I have grown worn out, will I have youth again? And my lord is old.”
The Lord said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh and say, ‘Will I really give birth, now that I am old?’”
“Is anything too great for the Lord? At this time I will return to you, while she is alive, and Sarah your wife will have a son.”
And Sarah denied it, saying, “I did not laugh,” because she was afraid. But he said, “No, you did laugh.”
And the men rose from there and looked toward Sodom. Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
The Lord said, “Shall I hide from my servant Abraham what I am doing?”
“Abraham will certainly become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed through him.”

“For I know him: he commands his children and his household after him to keep the ways of the Lord by doing what is right and just, so that the Lord may bring upon Abraham what he has promised concerning him.”
The Lord said, “The outcry from Sodom and Gomorrah has come up before me, and their sins have become very great.”
“I will go down and see whether they have acted fully according to the outcry that has come to me. If not, I will know.”
The men turned from there and went to Sodom, while Abraham was still standing before the Lord.
Abraham came near and said, “Will you destroy the righteous along with the wicked in the same outburst of anger?”
“If there are fifty righteous people within the city, will you destroy it in one outburst of anger? Will you not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous people within it?”

“Far be it from you to do such a thing—to kill the innocent along with the guilty, so that the innocent fare like the guilty! Far be it from you, Judge of all the earth! Such a judgment must not be carried out.”
The Lord said, “If I find fifty righteous people within the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake.”
Abraham answered and said, “Look, I have begun to speak before the Lord, though I am dust and ashes.”
“If there are five fewer than fifty righteous people, will you destroy the whole city because of those five?” He said, “I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there.”
Abraham spoke to him again and said, “What if forty are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy it if I find forty there.”
He said, “May the Lord not be angry, and let me speak. What if thirty are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy it if I find thirty there.”
He said, “Look, I have begun to speak before the Lord. What if twenty are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.”
He said, “Please do not let the Lord be angry, and let me speak just this once. What if ten are found there?” He said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.”
The Lord went away when he had finished speaking with Abraham, and Abraham returned to his own place.
The two angels came to Sodom in the evening, while Lot was sitting at the gate of Sodom. Lot saw them and rose to meet them, and bowed facedown to the ground.
He said, “Please, my lords, turn aside to your servant’s house. Spend the night and wash your feet. Then rise early and go on your way.” They said, “No, we will spend the night in the square.”
Lot urged them strongly, so they turned aside to him and entered his house. He prepared a feast for them and baked unleavened bread for them, and they ate.
Before they had lain down, the men of the town, the men of Sodom, surrounded the house, from young men to old men—all the people, without exception.
They called to Lot and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so that we can have sex with them.”
Lot went out to them at the doorway, and they closed the door behind him.
Lot said to them, “My brothers, do not do this evil.

Look, I have two daughters who have never had sex with a man. I will bring them out to you, and you may do to them whatever seems good to you. Only do nothing to these men, because they have come under the shelter of my roof.”

They said, “Get out of the way!” They also said, “This fellow came to live among us as a foreigner, and now he is judging us! Now we will treat you worse than them.” Lot struggled fiercely with the men, and they approached to break down the door.
The men reached out their hands and brought Lot into the house with them, and shut the door.
The men at the doorway of the house were struck with blindness, from the youngest to the oldest, and they wore themselves out trying to find the door.
The men said to Lot, “What are you doing here? Bring your sons-in-law, your sons, your daughters, and everyone you have in the town out of this place.
For we are going to destroy this place, because their outcry has risen before the Lord, and the Lord has sent us to destroy it.”

Lot went out and spoke with his sons-in-law, who had married his daughters. He said to them, “Get up! Get out of this place, because the Lord is going to destroy it.” But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking.
When dawn broke, the angels urged Lot, saying to him, “Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, so that you are not swept away because of the town’s sins.”
And Lot lingered. The angels took him by the hand, along with his wife and his two daughters, because the Lord had compassion on him. They brought him out and set him outside the town.
When they had brought them outside, they said to him, “Escape for your life! Do not look behind you, and do not stop anywhere in the plain. Escape to the mountain so that you do not perish.”
Lot said to them, “Please, my lords!
Your servant has found mercy in your eyes, and great is the kindness you have shown me by saving my life. But I cannot escape to the mountain, or disaster may overtake me and I will die.
Look, this town is near enough to flee to, and it is small. Let me escape there. Look, it is small, and my life will be spared.”
He said to him, “I have granted your request in this matter too: I will not overthrow the town you have spoken of.”
“Hurry and escape there, because I cannot do anything until you enter it.” For this reason he named the town Zoar.
The sun had risen over the land when Lot entered Zoar.
The Lord sent down sulfur and fire upon Sodom and Gomorrah, from the Lord out of heaven.
He overthrew those towns and the whole plain, all the inhabitants of the land, and everything that grew from the ground.
His wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
Abraham rose early in the morning and went to the place where he had stood before the Lord.
He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and toward all the land of the plain. He saw the smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
When God destroyed the towns of the plain, God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out from the midst of the destruction, when he overthrew the towns where Lot had lived.
Lot went up from Zoar and lived in the mountains, with his two daughters, because he was afraid to live in Zoar. He and his two daughters lived in a cave.
The older daughter said to the younger, “Look, our father is old, and there is no man in the land to have intercourse with us, as is the custom throughout the earth.
Come, let us give our father wine to drink and sleep with him, so that we may have offspring through our father.”
That night they gave their father wine to drink. The older daughter went in and slept with her father, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.

The next day, the older daughter said to the younger, “Look, I slept with my father last night. Let us give him wine to drink tonight too. Then go in and sleep with him, so that we may have offspring through our father.”
That night too they gave their father wine to drink. The younger daughter went in and slept with him, and he did not know when she lay down or when she got up.
And both of Lot’s daughters became pregnant by their father.
The older daughter gave birth to a son and named him Moab. He is the father of the Moabites to this day.
The younger daughter also gave birth to a son and named him Ben-ammi. He is the father of the Ammonites to this day.
Abraham moved on from there to the southern region and settled between Rekem and Gerar. Abraham lived as a foreigner in Gerar.
Abraham said of Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech, king of Gerar, sent for Sarah and took her.
And God came to Abimelech in a dream at night and said to him, “Look, you are going to die because of the woman you have taken, for she is another man’s wife.”
Abimelech had not approached her. Abimelech said, “Lord, will you kill even an innocent people?
He himself said, ‘She is my sister,’ and she herself also said, ‘He is my brother.’ I did this with an honest heart and clean hands.”
God said to him in a dream, “I too know that you did this with an honest heart. I myself kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Now return the man's wife, because he is a prophet. He will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not return her, know that you will certainly die, you and everyone who belongs to you.”
Abimelech rose early in the morning, called all his servants, and told them all these things. The men were very afraid.

Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, “What have I done to you, and how have I sinned against you, that you have brought such a great sin upon me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should never be done.”
Abimelech said to Abraham, “What did you see that made you do this?”
Abraham said, “Because I thought, ‘Perhaps there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.’
Besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father but not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife.
When God brought me out of my father's house, I said to her, ‘This is the kindness you must show me: wherever we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
Abimelech took sheep, cattle, male slaves, and female slaves and gave them to Abraham. He also returned Sarah his wife to him.
Abimelech said to Abraham, “Look, my land is before you. Settle wherever you please.”
To Sarah he said, “Look, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is also given to you because you covered the eyes of everyone with me, and you have rebuked me about everything.”
Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his slave women, and they bore children.
For the Lord had completely closed every womb in Abimelech’s household because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.
The Lord remembered Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did for Sarah as he had promised.
Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the time God had told him.
Abraham named his son who was born to him, whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.
Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
Sarah said, “God has brought me great joy today. Everyone who hears will rejoice with me.”
She said, “Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.”
The child grew and was weaned. Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
Sarah saw the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham mocking.
She said to Abraham, “Drive out this slave woman and her son, for this slave woman’s son will not inherit along with my son Isaac.”
This greatly distressed Abraham because it concerned his son.
And God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the boy and your slave woman. Listen to everything Sarah tells you, because it is through Isaac that your descendants will be named.”
“I will also make the slave woman’s son into a great nation, because he is your offspring.”

Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water, and gave them to Hagar. He put them on her shoulder, together with the boy, and sent her away. She left and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
The water in the skin ran out, and she put the boy under one of the bushes.
She went and sat opposite him, about a bowshot away, for she said, “Let me not see the boy die.” She sat opposite him, raised her voice, and wept.
God heard the boy’s voice, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, “What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the boy’s voice where he is.
Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him firmly with your hands, for I will make him into a great nation.”
And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the waterskin with water and gave the boy a drink.
God was with the boy. He grew up and lived in the wilderness of Paran, and he was learning archery.
In the wilderness of Paran. His mother found him a wife from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, “God is with you in everything you do.
Now swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me, my offspring, or my family. Show me and the land where you have lived the same kindness that I have shown you.”
Abraham said, “I will swear.”
Abraham rebuked Abimelech over the well of water that Abraham’s servants had dug and Abimelech’s servants had seized.
Abimelech said, “I do not know who did this. You did not tell me, and I have heard nothing about it until today.”
Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
Abraham set seven ewe lambs apart by themselves.
Abimelech said to Abraham, “What are these seven ewe lambs that you have set apart by themselves?”
He said, “Accept these seven ewe lambs from my hands, so that they may be a witness for me that I dug this well.”
For this reason he called that place Beersheba, because the two of them swore an oath there.
They made a covenant at Beersheba. Then Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tree at Beersheba and there called on the name of the Lord, the everlasting God.
And Abraham lived in the land of the Philistines for many days.
After these things, God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said to him, “Take your son, your only son, whom you love, Isaac, and go to the land of the Amorites. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I will tell you about.”

Abraham rose early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took two of his young servants with him, along with his son Isaac. He split wood for the burnt offering and set out for the place God had told him about.
On the third day, Abraham looked up and saw that place in the distance.
And he said to his servants, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there, worship, and return to you.”
Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and laid it on his son Isaac. He took the fire and the knife in his own hand, and the two of them went on together.
Isaac spoke to his father Abraham and said, “Father!” He said, “Here I am, my son.” Isaac said to him, “Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?”
Abraham said, “God will provide himself a lamb for the burnt offering, my son.” And the two of them went on together.
They came to the place God had told him about. Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
The angel of God called to him from heaven and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said, “Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him, because now you have shown that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”
Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide,” as it is said today, “On this mountain the Lord will provide.”
The angel of God called to Abraham from heaven a second time.
He said, “By myself I have sworn, says the Lord, because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”
I will surely bless you and greatly multiply your descendants, like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will possess the lands of their enemies.
Through your descendants all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed my voice.
Abraham returned to his young men, and they got up and went together to Beersheba. Abraham lived in Beersheba.
After these events, Abraham was told, “Look, Milcah too has borne sons to your brother Nahor:
Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.”
Bethuel fathered Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
His concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sarah’s life lasted one hundred and twenty-seven years. These were the years that Sarah lived.
Sarah died in the town of the giants, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
Abraham rose from beside his dead wife and spoke to the descendants of Heth, saying to them,
“I am a foreigner and a temporary resident among you. Give me a burial property among you so that I may bury my dead wife out of my sight.”
The descendants of Heth answered Abraham, saying,
“Listen to us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead wife in the best of our tombs. None of us will withhold his tomb from you for burying your dead wife.”
Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, the descendants of Heth.
He spoke to them and said, “If you are willing for me to bury my dead wife out of my sight, listen to me and intercede for me with Ephron son of Zohar,
so that he will give me his double cave at the edge of his field. Let him give it to me for the full price in silver, as a burial property among you.”
Ephron was sitting among the descendants of Heth. Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the presence of the descendants of Heth and everyone who entered the gate of his town, saying,
“No, my lord, listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave in it. In the presence of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead wife.”
Abraham bowed before the people of the land.

He said to Ephron in the presence of the people of the land, “If you are willing, listen to me. I will give you the silver for the price of the field. Take it from me, and I will bury my dead wife there.”
Ephron answered Abraham, saying,
“My lord, listen to me. The land is worth four hundred shekels of silver. What is that between you and me? Bury your dead wife.”

Abraham agreed with Ephron, and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver he had specified in the presence of the descendants of Heth: four hundred shekels of silver at the weight accepted by merchants.
So Ephron’s field at the double cave opposite Mamre was confirmed—the field of the cave, the cave in it, and all the trees in the field within its boundaries all around.
They were sold to Abraham in the presence of the Hittites and everyone entering the gate of his town.
Afterward Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave in the field of Machpelah, opposite Mamre—that is, Hebron—in the land of Canaan.
The field of the cave and the cave in it were transferred from the Hittites to Abraham as a burial property.
Abraham was old and advanced in years, and the Lord had blessed Abraham in everything.
Abraham called his elderly servant, the manager of his household, who was in charge of everything he owned, and said to him, “Put your hand under my loins.
I will make you swear by the Lord, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I live.
Instead, go to my country and my relatives, and take a wife for my son Isaac.”
The servant said to him, “What if the woman is unwilling to follow me to this land? Should I then take your son back to the land you came from?”
Abraham said to him, “Be careful not to take my son back there.

The Lord, the God of heaven, who brought me from there, from my father’s house and the land of my birth, who spoke to me and promised me, ‘I will give this land to your descendants,’ will send his angel ahead of you, and you will take a wife for my son from there.
If the woman will not agree to come with you, you will be free from this oath to me. Only do not take my son back there.”
The servant put his hand under the loins of Abraham his master and swore to him concerning this matter.
The servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed, taking all kinds of his master’s valuables with him. He set out and went to Aram-naharaim, to the town of Nahor.
He made his camels kneel outside the town beside the well of water, in the evening, at the time when the women came out to draw water.
He prayed and said, “Lord, God of my master Abraham, make things go well for me today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
Here I am, standing beside the well of water, and the daughters of the townspeople are coming out to draw water.”

“And the young woman to whom I say, ‘Lower your jar for me so that I may drink,’ and who says to me, ‘Drink, and I will also water your camels’—let her be the one you have prepared for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you are showing kindness and faithfulness to my master.”
He had not yet finished speaking when Rebekah came out, with her water jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor.
The young woman was very beautiful, a virgin who had never had sexual relations with a man. She went down to the well, filled her jar, and came back up.
The servant ran to meet her and said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink from your jar.”
She said to him, “Drink, my lord.” She quickly lowered her jar onto her hands and gave him a drink.
When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will draw water for your camels too, until they have finished drinking.”
She quickly emptied her jar into the watering trough and ran back to the well to draw water. She drew water for all his camels.
The man was [?] and watching her closely, waiting to find out whether the Lord had made his journey successful or not.
When the camels had finished drinking, the servant took a gold earring weighing one shekel and two bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels of gold.
He said to her, “Tell me, whose daughter are you? Is there room for us to spend the night in your father’s house?”
She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, Milcah’s son, whom she bore to Nahor.”
She also said to him, “We have plenty of straw and fodder, and also a place to spend the night.”
The man knelt on the ground and worshiped the Lord.

He said, “Blessed is the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld his kindness and faithfulness from my master. The Lord has guided me on the way to the house of my master’s brother, to take my master’s brother’s daughter as a wife for his son.”
The girl ran and told her father’s household these things.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban. Laban ran outside to the man at the well.

When he saw the earrings and the bracelets on his sister’s wrists, and when he heard his sister Rebekah’s words, “This is what the man said to me,” he came to the man, who was standing beside the camels at the well.
He said to him, “Come in, you who are blessed by the Lord. Why are you standing outside? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.”
The man entered the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and fodder were put out for the camels, and water was brought to wash his feet and the feet of the men with him.
They set food before them, but he said, “I will not eat until I have said what I have to say.” They said to him, “Speak.”
He said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
The Lord has blessed my master, and he has become very great. He has acquired sheep, cattle, silver, gold, male and female servants, female donkeys, camels, and donkeys.
Sarah, my master’s wife, bore my master a son after she had grown old, and he has given him everything he has.
My master made me swear an oath and said to me, ‘Do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live.
Instead, go to my father’s household and to my family, and take a wife for my son from there.’
I said to my master, ‘What if the woman is unwilling to come with me?’
My master said to me, ‘The Lord, whom I have served, will send his angel with you and make your journey successful. You will take a wife for my son from my family and from my father’s household.
Then you will be released from my oaths when you go to my family. If they will not give her to you, you will be released from my oaths.’
Today I came to the well and said, ‘Lord, God of my master Abraham, if you will make the journey I have undertaken successful:
Here I am standing beside the well of water. When a young woman comes out to draw water, and I say to her, “Please give me a little water to drink from your jar,”
and she says to me, “Drink, and I will draw water for your camels too,” she is the woman whom the Lord has prepared for my master’s son.’

Before I had finished speaking in my heart, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and filled it. I said to her, ‘Please give me a little water to drink from your jar.’
She quickly lowered her jar and said to me, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels too.’ I drank, and she also watered my camels.
I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ She said, ‘I am the daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ I put bracelets on her wrists and earrings in her ears.

I bowed down and worshiped the Lord. I blessed the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, who had guided me on the right path to the house of my master’s brother, to take my master’s brother’s daughter as a wife for his son.
Now, if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me. If not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left.
Laban and Bethuel answered, “This matter has come from the Lord. We cannot say anything good or bad to you.
Here is Rebekah before you. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, as the Lord has said.”
When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed down to the ground before the Lord.
The servant brought out gold and silver articles and clothing and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave gifts to her brothers and her mother.
He and the men with him ate and drank and stayed the night. He rose early in the morning and said to them, “Send me back to my master.”
Her brothers and her mother said to him, “Let the young woman stay with us for a full month. Then she may go.”
He said to them, “Do not delay me, since the Lord has made my journey successful. Send me on my way so that I may go to my master.”
They said, “Let us call the girl and ask her directly.”
They called Rebekah and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” She said, “I will go.”
So they sent away their sister Rebekah and her nurse, along with Abraham’s servant and his men.
They blessed their sister Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become thousands and tens of thousands, and may your descendants possess the lands of their enemies.”
Rebekah and her young women got up, mounted the camels, and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
Isaac was coming from Beer-lahai-roi. He was living in the southern region.
Isaac went out to walk in the field toward evening. He looked up and saw camels coming.
Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, and she leaned down on the camel.
She said to the servant, “Who is this man coming through the field to meet us?” The servant said, “He is my master.” Then she took her veil and covered herself.
The servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah. He married Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. Isaac was comforted after the loss of his mother.
And Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.
She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were the Asshurim, the Letushim, and the Leummim.
The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were Keturah’s children.
Abraham gave everything he owned to his son Isaac.
Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubine. While he was still alive, he sent them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the land of the east.
And these were the years of Abraham’s life that he lived: one hundred and seventy-five years.
Abraham became ill and died at a good old age, old and full of days, and was gathered to his people.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the double cave in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, opposite Mamre.
This was the field Abraham had bought from the Hittites as a burial property. Abraham and his wife Sarah were buried there.
After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac. Isaac lived beside Beer-lahai-roi.
And these are the descendants of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s slave woman, bore to Abraham.
These are the names of Ishmael’s sons, listed by name according to their generations: Ishmael’s firstborn Nebaioth, then Kedar, Arbel, and Mibsam.
And Mishma, Ruma, and Massa.
And Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
These are Ishmael’s sons, and these are their names according to their settlements and encampments: twelve chiefs of their peoples.
Ishmael lived 137 years. He became ill and died and was gathered to his people.
They settled from Havilah to Shud, which is opposite Egypt, on the way to Assyria. He settled along the border of all his brothers.
These are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son. Abraham fathered Isaac.
Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram and the sister of Laban the Aramean.
